config.borderlesswindow.title: Borderless Window Settings
borderlesswindow.options.screen_mode.too: Choose between a normal window, borderless fullscreen, or Minecraft's regular exclusive fullscreen.
borderlesswindow.options.vanilla.inactiv: Replaced by Borderless Window's Idle FPS Limit while that is on: its limits take the place of the "AFK" setting, and Minecraft still caps a minimized game at 10 FPS. Turn the Idle FPS Limit off to use this option again.
borderlesswindow.options.sodium.inactivi: While Borderless Window's Idle FPS Limit is on, this option is replaced by it and greyed out.
borderlesswindow.options.vanilla.open_co: Every Borderless Window option: F11, the held item name, the FPS counter and background limits, enchantments, fog, clouds, sky and weather, screen overlays, camera, zoom and distances. With Sodium installed, they are in its video settings instead.
borderlesswindow.options.f11_mode.name: F11 Mode
borderlesswindow.options.f11_mode.toolti: What the F11 key does: toggle borderless fullscreen, toggle Minecraft's regular exclusive fullscreen, or cycle through all three screen modes.
The name of the item you switch to, shown above the hotbar for a couple of seconds. Turn Off to keep that space clear. The name can still be seen in the inventory or by hovering over the item.
borderlesswindow.options.fast_language_r: Changes the language as soon as you click Done, without the loading screen. Minecraft normally reloads every texture, model and sound just to change the language. The search in the creative inventory and in JEI, REI and EMI switches to the new language too. Other mods with their own search may keep the previous language until the next full reload; press F3+T to force one. Turn Off to switch languages the way Minecraft does.
borderlesswindow.options.toast_advanceme: The pop-up in the top-right corner when you make an advancement. Turn Off to hide it; the advancement still counts and chat announces it as usual. The challenge fanfare plays with the pop-up, so it goes too.
borderlesswindow.options.toast_recipes.t: The pop-up when you unlock new recipes. Turn Off to hide it; the recipes are still added to the recipe book.
The tutorial hints for new players (moving, punching a tree, opening the inventory, crafting planks) and the reminder of the Social Interactions key the first time you join a server. Turn Off to hide them.
borderlesswindow.options.toast_unverifie: The "Chat messages can't be verified" pop-up when joining a server that does not enforce secure chat. Turn Off to hide it; chat works the same.
The pop-up when the narrator is turned on or off, for example with Ctrl+B.
borderlesswindow.options.toast_pack_down: The progress pop-up while a server's resource pack downloads. Turn Off to hide it; if a download fails, the pop-up still shows. Error pop-ups (resource packs that fail to load, worlds that cannot be opened, low disk space) always show.
borderlesswindow.options.vanilla_menu_bl: Minecraft's own Menu Background Blur slider: how much the world is blurred behind menus and inventories. Sodium's video settings leave it out, so it is brought back here. It is the same setting found under Accessibility and is saved with Minecraft's options, not the mod's.
borderlesswindow.options.vanilla_damage_: Minecraft's own Damage Tilt slider: how much the camera shakes when you take damage. Sodium's video settings leave it out, so it is brought back here. It is the same setting found under Accessibility and is saved with Minecraft's options, not the mod's.
borderlesswindow.options.vanilla_darknes: Minecraft's own Darkness Pulsing slider: how strongly the screen pulses with the Darkness effect a Warden or a Sculk Shrieker gives you. Sodium's video settings leave it out, so it is brought back here. It is the same setting found under Accessibility and is saved with Minecraft's options, not the mod's.
borderlesswindow.options.vanilla_hide_li: Minecraft's own Hide Lightning Flashes option: when On, lightning no longer lights up the whole sky. The bolts themselves are still drawn. Sodium's video settings leave it out, so it is brought back here. It is the same setting found under Accessibility and is saved with Minecraft's options, not the mod's.
borderlesswindow.options.fps_overlay_mod: Shows an FPS counter on screen. Simple displays only the current FPS; Extended shows a single line with the current FPS plus the Min, Avg and Max FPS over the last 15 seconds. The overlay hides itself while the debug screen (F3) is open or the GUI is hidden (F1).
borderlesswindow.options.fps_overlay_pos: Corner of the screen where the FPS overlay is drawn.
borderlesswindow.options.unfocused_fps_l: Caps the frame rate while the game window is not focused: after Alt+Tab, when it is minimized, or when you click another window or monitor. Saves GPU power and heat while the game sits in the background. Off keeps the vanilla behavior, rendering at full speed. A lower regular Max Framerate still wins. The cap lifts as soon as you click back into the game.
Lowers the frame rate after this many minutes without keyboard or mouse input, even while the game window is focused. Useful when you step away from the computer with the game open. Any key, click, scroll or mouse movement lifts the limit at once. While it is on, it replaces the "AFK" setting of Minecraft's Reduce FPS When option; Minecraft still caps a minimized game at 10 FPS. Off keeps the vanilla behavior.
The frame rate cap applied once the idle time above has passed. A lower regular Max Framerate or Unfocused FPS Limit still wins.
borderlesswindow.options.idle_fps_second: Adds a second step to the idle limit: after this many minutes without keyboard or mouse input, the Second Idle FPS Limit applies. Always longer than the first idle time; both count from your last input. Needs the first idle limit to be on. Off keeps a single step.
The frame rate cap applied once the second idle time has passed. If it is higher than the first idle cap, the lower one still wins.
borderlesswindow.options.minimized_skip_: Stops drawing frames while the game window is minimized; the game loop keeps running, 10 times per second, as Minecraft does when minimized. Nothing else changes: sounds and multiplayer connections carry on, and a single-player world pauses just as it does without the mod; only the picture stops until you restore the window. Saves more GPU power than the unfocused FPS limit. Off keeps the vanilla behavior.
borderlesswindow.options.unfocused_volum: Lowers the game volume while its window is not focused: after Alt+Tab, when it is minimized, or when you click another window or monitor. It is a share of your Master Volume; Muted silences the game entirely. 100%% keeps the vanilla behavior. Full volume returns as soon as you click back into the game.
borderlesswindow.options.fog_terrain.too: The atmospheric haze that fades out distant terrain, including the Nether's thick fog. Turn Off for a clearer view into the distance. Fog from the Blindness and Darkness effects is never affected by these toggles.
borderlesswindow.options.fog_water.name: Water Fog
borderlesswindow.options.fog_water.toolt: The fog seen while underwater. Turn Off to see much farther when diving.
borderlesswindow.options.fog_lava.name: Lava Fog
borderlesswindow.options.fog_lava.toolti: The fog seen while submerged in lava. Turn Off to see through lava while inside it.
borderlesswindow.options.fog_powder_snow: The fog seen while inside powder snow. Turn Off to keep your view clear.
borderlesswindow.options.fog_terrain_sta: Where the distance fog begins, as a share of your render distance. Default is Minecraft's own: the fog only covers about the last tenth (around 90%%). Lower values start it closer, for a softer and deeper haze; 95%% pushes it to the very edge. The far end always stays at your render distance. Only the ordinary terrain fog moves: the Nether's thick fog, water, lava, and Blindness or Darkness are left alone.
borderlesswindow.options.cloud_height.to: Raises or lowers the cloud layer, between y=64 and y=320. "Default" leaves each dimension's own height untouched, and "(Regular)" marks Minecraft's own, which is 192. Dimensions with no clouds at all — the Nether, the End, cloudless dimensions from other mods — stay that way at any setting: this moves clouds, it never adds them.
borderlesswindow.options.sky_sun_moon.to: Draws the sun and the moon. Turn Off to hide them: day still turns into night as usual, and sunrises and sunsets keep their colors. With shaders, packs that draw their own sun and moon keep them: look for that in the pack's settings.
borderlesswindow.options.sky_stars.name: Stars
borderlesswindow.options.sky_stars.toolt: Draws the stars in the night sky. Turn Off for a plain dark sky. With shaders, packs that draw their own stars keep them: look for that in the pack's settings.
borderlesswindow.options.sky_weather.too: Draws the rain and snow falling around you. Turn Off to hide them: it still rains, so mobs, crops and fishing behave as usual, and the rain sounds and the splashes on the ground stay. The sky still darkens during storms.
borderlesswindow.options.overlay_water.t: The rippling texture drawn over your view while underwater. Turn Off for a clear view while swimming. This is separate from Water Fog, which controls how far you can see rather than what is drawn on the screen.
borderlesswindow.options.overlay_fire.to: The flames drawn across your view while you are burning. Turn Off to keep your view clear while on fire. The suffocation overlay shown when your head is inside a solid block is never affected.
borderlesswindow.options.overlay_fire_sm: Keeps the fire overlay, but hides it while you have Fire Resistance. Minecraft draws that same overlay while you swim in lava, so this also clears your view inside lava for as long as the effect lasts. Requires the Fire Overlay to be On.
borderlesswindow.options.overlay_fire_he: How high the flames reach over your view while you are burning. 100%% is Minecraft's own height; lower values push them down toward the bottom of the screen, so they cover less of it and you still notice you are on fire. Requires the Fire Overlay to be On. The Smart Fire Overlay still applies.
borderlesswindow.options.overlay_pumpkin: The blur drawn around your view while wearing a carved pumpkin. Turn Off to see normally, so a pumpkin can be worn against endermen without the visual cost. Helmet overlays added by other mods are never affected.
The frost border drawn around your view while freezing in powder snow. Turn Off to keep your view clear. Note this border is also a warning that you are taking freeze damage; the frozen hearts on the HUD still show it.
The purple warp drawn over your view while standing inside a Nether portal. Turn Off to see clearly while building or aligning portals.
borderlesswindow.options.overlay_spyglas: The scope texture and the black bars drawn while looking through a spyglass. Turn Off to keep the zoom across the whole screen. The zoom itself is unchanged; only the frame around it is removed.
borderlesswindow.options.overlay_totem.t: The Totem of Undying that pops up over the screen when one saves you. Turn Off to keep your view clear at that moment; the totem's particles and sound still play. Items from other mods that use the same animation are hidden too.
borderlesswindow.options.night_vision.to: How Night Vision behaves in its last 10 seconds. Flicker: Minecraft's own, the screen pulses between bright and dark as a warning. Fade Out: the brightness goes down smoothly and reaches darkness just as the effect ends. Steady: full brightness until the end. How long the effect lasts never changes.
borderlesswindow.options.effect_particle: The swirls your own potion and status effects spawn around you, which float through your view in first person. Turn Off to remove them for you, in first and third person. Other players and mobs keep theirs, and other players still see yours.
borderlesswindow.options.nametags.name: Nametags
borderlesswindow.options.nametags.toolti: Which names are drawn above entities. All: Minecraft's own. Players Only: only other players' names. Mobs Only: only the names of everything else (named mobs and pets, and also named armor stands, which servers often use for floating text). None: no nametags. The names are only hidden from view; chat, the player list and death messages still show them.
borderlesswindow.options.camera_bob.name: Camera Bobbing
borderlesswindow.options.camera_bob.tool: How much the camera sways as you walk. Full is vanilla. Vertical Only keeps the up-and-down bounce but removes the side-to-side sway and the tilt, so the horizon stays level -- the tilt is what most people find nauseating. Off holds the camera still. Requires Minecraft's own View Bobbing option to be on.
borderlesswindow.options.hand_bob.name: Hand Bobbing
borderlesswindow.options.hand_bob.toolti: Whether the held item sways as you walk, controlled separately from the camera. Turn Off for a steady hand while keeping camera movement, or leave On with the camera off. Requires Minecraft's own View Bobbing option to be on.
borderlesswindow.options.vanilla_fov.too: Minecraft's own FOV Effects slider, which scales all four options below at once. Sodium's video settings leave it out, so this brings it back here. It is the same setting as the one in Accessibility Settings and is saved with Minecraft's options, not the mod's.
borderlesswindow.options.fov_speed.name: Speed FOV
borderlesswindow.options.fov_speed.toolt: How much the view widens as you move faster -- sprinting, Speed potions, anything that raises movement speed. 100%% is vanilla. Minecraft has one slider for all four of these together; here they are separate. Requires Minecraft's own FOV Effects to be on.
borderlesswindow.options.fov_flying.name: Flying FOV
borderlesswindow.options.fov_flying.tool: The extra widening while flying in creative. Elytra gliding is not affected -- that is not the same flying. It is a small 10%% pull, and sprint speed usually masks it. Requires Minecraft's own FOV Effects to be on.
borderlesswindow.options.fov_bow.name: Bow FOV
borderlesswindow.options.fov_bow.tooltip: The zoom that builds up while you draw a bow. 100%% is vanilla, 0%% holds the view still. The spyglass is never affected: its zoom is what the item does, not a visual effect. Requires Minecraft's own FOV Effects to be on.
borderlesswindow.options.fov_fluid.name: Fluid FOV
borderlesswindow.options.fov_fluid.toolt: The squeeze applied while your head is in water or lava. 100%% is vanilla. Requires Minecraft's own FOV Effects to be on.
borderlesswindow.options.vanilla_distort: Minecraft's own Distortion Effects slider, which scales both options below at once. Sodium's video settings leave it out, so this brings it back here. It is the same setting as the one in Accessibility Settings and is saved with Minecraft's options, not the mod's. Lowering it also brings back the green nausea texture, which is Minecraft's replacement cue.
borderlesswindow.options.distortion_port: How much the view warps while you stand in a Nether portal. 100%% is vanilla. Minecraft has one slider for this and for Nausea together; here they are separate. Sits under Minecraft's own Distortion Effects slider: with that at Off, nothing warps and this has no effect.
borderlesswindow.options.distortion_naus: How much the view warps while you have the Nausea effect, from a potion, a pufferfish or suspicious stew. 100%% is vanilla. Sits under Minecraft's own Distortion Effects slider: with that at Off, nothing warps and this has no effect.
borderlesswindow.options.zoom_mode.name: Zoom Key
borderlesswindow.options.zoom_mode.toolt: How the Zoom key works. It is C by default and can be changed in Minecraft's Controls. Hold zooms only while the key is held down; Toggle zooms in with one press and out with the next. While you look through a spyglass the zoom steps aside: the spyglass keeps its own.
borderlesswindow.options.zoom_level.name: Zoom Level
borderlesswindow.options.zoom_level.tool: How much the view is magnified every time you start zooming: at 4× you see a quarter of your usual field of view. The mouse turns slower in the same proportion, so aiming feels the same. Only the field of view changes: nothing is drawn any farther away.
borderlesswindow.options.zoom_scroll.too: While zooming, the mouse wheel zooms further in or back out, from 1× to 50×, instead of changing the hotbar slot. The next zoom starts again at the Zoom Level.
borderlesswindow.options.zoom_smooth.too: Eases in and out of the zoom instead of jumping straight to it.
Hides the held item while zooming, so it does not cover the view.
borderlesswindow.options.zoom_hide_hud.t: Hides the HUD while zooming, as if you pressed F1: hotbar, crosshair, chat and everything else.
borderlesswindow.options.enchantment_lev: How enchantment levels are written next to the enchantment name. Minecraft only has Roman numerals up to X and shows raw text like "enchantment.level.11" above that. Mixed keeps the Roman numerals and switches to plain numbers past X; the other two use a single style at every level. Levels go up to 255.
borderlesswindow.options.vanilla_glint_s: Minecraft's own Glint Speed slider: how fast the shimmer moves across enchanted items. Sodium's video settings leave it out, so it is brought back here. It is the same setting found under Accessibility and is saved with Minecraft's options, not the mod's.

Minecraft's own Glint Strength slider: how visible the shimmer on enchanted items is. Off hides it entirely. Sodium's video settings leave it out, so it is brought back here. It is the same setting found under Accessibility and is saved with Minecraft's options, not the mod's.
borderlesswindow.options.distance_entiti: How far away entities are drawn: mobs, animals, dropped items, item frames, boats and the rest. Every kind below follows this slider while it is set to General, or can have its own distance instead. Minecraft's distance depends on each entity's size and its Entity Distance option, and ends where the server stops sending them, usually 64 to 160 blocks. Default keeps Minecraft's distance. Entities are only hidden: they keep moving and can still hurt you. Other players, glowing entities and floating text (armor stands with a visible name, text displays) are always drawn.
borderlesswindow.options.distance_hostil: How far away hostile mobs are drawn: zombies, skeletons, creepers, endermen, piglins, and hostile water mobs such as guardians and drowned. Mobs from other mods go by the category their mod gives them. They are only hidden: they keep moving and can still hurt you. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for these mobs, higher or lower.
borderlesswindow.options.distance_land_a: How far away land animals are drawn: cows, pigs, sheep, chickens, wolves, bees, foxes, parrots, bats, and also frogs and turtles, which Minecraft counts here. Lower it for animal farms. Mobs from other mods go by the category their mod gives them. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for these mobs, higher or lower.
borderlesswindow.options.distance_water_: How far away peaceful water mobs are drawn: dolphins, squid, glow squid, fish and axolotls. Guardians and drowned are Hostile Mobs, as Minecraft classifies them. Mobs from other mods go by the category their mod gives them. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for these mobs, higher or lower.
borderlesswindow.options.distance_villag: How far away villagers, wandering traders, iron golems and snow golems are drawn. Lower it for trading halls and iron farms. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for these mobs, higher or lower.
How far away dropped items are drawn. Minecraft draws them up to 16 blocks away, more if you raise its Entity Distance option. Lower it to cut the cost of item farms and messy storage rooms. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for items, higher or lower. Items are only hidden, never removed: they are still there and can be picked up. Glowing items are always drawn.
borderlesswindow.options.distance_xp_orb: How far away experience orbs are drawn. Minecraft draws them up to 32 blocks away, more if you raise its Entity Distance option. Lower it for mob farms that leave a cloud of orbs behind. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for orbs, higher or lower. Orbs are only hidden: they still fly to you and give experience.
borderlesswindow.options.distance_armor_: How far away armor stands are drawn. Minecraft draws them as far as the server sends them, around 160 blocks. Lower it for bases and builds full of displayed armor. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for armor stands, higher or lower. Armor stands with a visible name are always drawn, since servers and maps use them for floating text and holograms.
borderlesswindow.options.distance_frames: How far away item frames (with the item in them) and paintings are drawn. Minecraft draws item frames as far as the server sends them, around 160 blocks. Lower it for walls of framed items in storage rooms and shops. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for these, higher or lower.
borderlesswindow.options.distance_vehicl: How far away boats and minecarts are drawn, including minecarts with chests, hoppers or TNT. Lower it for rail systems and boat docks. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for these, higher or lower.
borderlesswindow.options.distance_projec: How far away projectiles are drawn: arrows (also the ones stuck in blocks), tridents, snowballs, fireballs and fireworks. The server sends them up to 64 blocks away. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for projectiles, higher or lower.
borderlesswindow.options.distance_block_: How far away blocks with their own model are drawn: chests, signs, banners, heads, beds and the rest below. Every kind below follows this slider while it is set to General, or can have its own distance instead. Minecraft always draws them up to 64 blocks, and none of its options changes that. Default keeps Minecraft's distance. They are only hidden: they are still there and work as usual. Beacons, End portals and gateways, and moving pistons are always drawn.
borderlesswindow.options.distance_chests: How far away chests, trapped chests, ender chests and shulker boxes are drawn. Lower it for storage rooms full of chests. Past the distance the whole chest disappears, not just its lid. Barrels are ordinary blocks and are not affected. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for these, higher or lower.
How far away signs and hanging signs are drawn, text included. Lower it for shops and labeled storage. Past the distance the whole sign disappears, not just its text. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for signs, higher or lower.
borderlesswindow.options.distance_banner: How far away banners are drawn, standing or on walls. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for banners, higher or lower.
How far away mob and player heads are drawn. Lower it for head collections and decorated builds. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for heads, higher or lower.
borderlesswindow.options.distance_beds.t: How far away beds are drawn. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for beds, higher or lower.
How far away the books on lecterns and enchanting tables are drawn. Only the book disappears; the lectern or the table stays. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for books, higher or lower.
How far away bells are drawn. Only the bell disappears; its frame or post stays. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for bells, higher or lower.
borderlesswindow.options.distance_campfi: How far away the food cooking on campfires is drawn. Only the food disappears; the campfire and its flames stay. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for campfire food, higher or lower.
borderlesswindow.options.distance_pots.t: How far away decorated pots are drawn. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for pots, higher or lower.
borderlesswindow.options.distance_spawne: How far away the spinning mob inside spawners and trial spawners, and the item inside vaults, are drawn. Only what is inside disappears; the cage stays. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for these, higher or lower.
borderlesswindow.options.distance_partic: How far away new particles can appear: smoke, redstone, explosions, potion effects and the rest below, plus any particle without a group of its own, such as biome ambience and particles from other mods. Every kind below follows this slider while it is set to General, or can have its own distance instead. Minecraft allows most particles up to 32 blocks away. Default keeps Minecraft's distance. Lower it to cut the cost of farms, redstone and big fights. Block breaking and firework sparks are never affected. Works on top of Minecraft's Particles option.

How far away smoke and flames can appear: torches, furnaces, campfires (their smoke columns too), candles, fire and lava. Lower it for bases full of torches and furnaces. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for these particles, higher or lower.

How far away redstone particles can appear: powered dust, redstone torches, repeaters and lit redstone ore. Lower it for large contraptions. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for these particles, higher or lower.

How far away explosions can appear: TNT, creepers, wind charges and breezes, and the puff a mob leaves when it dies. Minecraft shows these past its usual 32 blocks. Lower it for creeper and TNT farms and mob grinders. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for these particles, higher or lower.

How far away effect particles can appear: the swirls around anyone under a potion or beacon effect, splash and lingering potions, witches, dragon's breath and omens. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for these particles, higher or lower.

How far away combat particles can appear: critical hits, enchanted hits, sweep attacks, the damage hearts and the Warden's sonic boom. Lower it for mob farms and big fights. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for these particles, higher or lower.

How far away water particles can appear: rain hitting the ground, splashes, bubbles and bubble columns, fishing, conduits, and every drip (water, lava, honey, crying obsidian, dripstone). Lower it for bubble elevators and rainy weather. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for these particles, higher or lower.

How far away the particles mobs give off can appear: breeding hearts, villagers' green and angry particles (bone meal's sparkles share them), note blocks, squid ink, llama spit, panda sneezes, slimes, dolphins and bees. Lower it for animal and villager farms. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for these particles, higher or lower.

How far away portal particles can appear: Nether portals, endermen, ender pearls, ender chests and charged respawn anchors. Lower it for portal hubs and enderman farms. General follows the General slider; any other value replaces it for these particles, higher or lower.
